cleanIntro: The DUAL-LOK 5 AM is an additive-manufactured can in Griffin's Nickel 625X alloy, on Griffin's DUAL-LOK mount: it threads onto a DUAL-LOK muzzle device and a spring-loaded collar locks over the mount's tines. Griffin's book prints no way of taking the can apart, and says the mount itself is not user serviceable. Its cleaning is done with the can off the rifle: after every use the mount interface is cleaned and given fresh anti-seize, and carbon is brushed off the muzzle device. Every 4,000 rounds the can is soaked in a mild solvent — that is the deep clean. How your rifle is unloaded comes from that rifle's own manual.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber clear
steps.action: Before any maintenance, take the magazine out of the rifle and clear the chamber, following the rifle's own manual for how that is done and checked.
steps.prose: Griffin's book covers the suppressor, not the rifle it sits on: the rifle's unloading steps come from the rifle's manufacturer.
steps.aside: First, clear your firearm in accordance with it’s manufacturers user manual.
steps.quote: ALWAYS REMOVE THE MAGAZINE FROM THE FIREARM AND CLEAR THE CHAMBER BEFORE PERFORMING ANY MAINTENANCE OPERATION
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — PREPARATION & PRECAUTIONS, p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Let it cool all the way down
steps.action: When you have finished firing, let the suppressor cool to the temperature of the room before you touch the collar or try to take it off.
steps.prose: A can that has just been shot looks exactly like a cold one, and this one gets hot enough to burn badly through a glove.
steps.quote: Once done firing, ALLOW SUPPRESSOR TO COOL to ambient temperature.
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — MOUNTING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.8
steps.warn: Material temperatures can reach in excess of 1000°F under normal use.

steps.title: Unlock the collar
steps.action: Once the can is cool, push the collar down toward the rifle — you will feel the wave spring compress — and turn it left or right until it finds the neutral, unlocked position. The mount's tines show when it is unlocked.
steps.prose: If the collar will not move, it is not yet pushed far enough against its spring; do not grip the can with a tool to force it.
steps.aside: Tines will be exposed in this position.
steps.quote: After the suppressor has cooled, push down the collar which will compress the wave spring and turn either left or right to find the neutral position (Fig. UNLOCKED).
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — MOUNTING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.8

steps.title: Unscrew the can from the muzzle device
steps.action: With the collar unlocked, unscrew the suppressor all the way off the muzzle device. Griffin advises storing it with the collar in the locked position so the tines are protected while it is handled.
steps.prose: The muzzle device stays on the rifle: it was timed with shims and torqued when it was mounted, and none of the cleaning needs it off. If yours is the HUB-mount version on another company's mount, that mount's own manual governs how the can comes off.
steps.aside: It is advised to store the suppressor in the locked configuration as this will protect the tines from the possible abuse of daily handling.
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — MOUNTING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.8

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes
steps.action: With the can off the rifle the strip is done. Griffin prints no procedure for taking the can apart, and its book says the DUAL-LOK mount must not be taken apart or modified at all.
steps.prose: Anything past this point belongs to Griffin's technical service department.
steps.aside: This should only be done by Griffin’s technical service department in the highly unlikely event it is necessary.
steps.quote: This mount is not end user serviceable. It should not be disassembled or modified in any way, or this will void the warranty.
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — MOUNTING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.8

steps.title: Clean the mount interface and re-apply anti-seize
steps.action: After every use, clean the mount interface inside the back of the suppressor and put a fresh, light coat of high-temperature anti-seize on its internal taper.
steps.prose: This is what stops the can seizing onto the muzzle device; a light coat is enough to make it come off easily after heavy use.
steps.aside: The Anti Seize should be used on the internal taper of the suppressor.
steps.quote: Clean and re-apply Anti Seize to the mount interface of the silencer after every use to prevent your suppressor from becoming stuck on the muzzle device.
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — CLEANING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.9

steps.title: A 1-inch pipe brush inside the mount — nothing coarser
steps.action: Use a 1-inch pipe-cleaning brush to clean inside the suppressor's mount interface. Do not use a coarse or medium wire wheel or brush on the mount.
steps.prose: Griffin's tool kit names the 1-inch maintenance pipe brush as all that is needed for the mount's bore, taper and threads.
steps.quote: An Oatey 1” pipe cleaning brush can be used to clean the inside mount interface of the suppressor.
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — CLEANING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.9
steps.warn: DO NOT USE course or medium wire wheels or brushes, as this can cause damage to your mount.

steps.title: Brush the carbon off the muzzle device
steps.action: With a fine wire brush or wheel, take the excess carbon off the outside of the muzzle device that is still on the rifle.
steps.prose: Carbon left on the device is what the can has to seat over next time. The device is hard tool steel, but take care not to mar its finish or its wrench flats.
steps.quote: Remove excess carbon from the muzzle device OD with a fine wire brush or wheel.
steps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — CLEANING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.9

deepSteps.title: Soak the can in a mild solvent
deepSteps.action: Every 4,000 rounds, with the suppressor off the rifle, soak it in a mild cleaning solvent such as Kroil to stop carbon building up inside.
deepSteps.prose: Nothing comes apart for this: the can is soaked whole. Griffin names Kroil as an example of a mild solvent.
deepSteps.quote: The Silencer should be soaked in a mild cleaning solvent, such as Kroil, every 4000 rounds to prevent carbon buildup
deepSteps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — CLEANING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.9

deepSteps.title: Drain it, then 30 rounds to blow out the rest
deepSteps.action: Take the can out of the solvent and let it drain. Once it is back on the rifle, fire 30 rounds through it to blow out any solvent left inside.
deepSteps.prose: Expect those first rounds to smoke. Clean and re-grease the mount interface with anti-seize before it goes back on, as after every use.
deepSteps.quote: then drained and shot 30 rounds to blow out any excess solvent.
deepSteps.cite: Griffin Armament DUAL-LOK AM Suppressors — Owners Manual (Installation & Maintenance Guide) — UNKNOWN — no edition printed in the document; file name DUAL-LOK-AM-Manual_2026 — CLEANING THE SUPPRESSOR, p.9

cleaning.name: MOUNT INTERFACE
tasks: Mount interface inside the can cleaned with a 1-inch pipe brush
Fresh light coat of high-temperature anti-seize on the internal taper
Do not use a coarse or medium wire wheel or brush on the mount

cleaning.name: MUZZLE DEVICE
tasks: Excess carbon brushed off the outside of the muzzle device with a fine wire brush or wheel
Device left on the rifle: its timing and torque are not disturbed

reassembly: Can drained of solvent; mount interface cleaned and given a light coat of high-temperature anti-seize.
Rifle unloaded: magazine out, chamber clear.
Make sure the DUAL-LOK collar is in the UNLOCKED position — installing it locked damages the system.
Thread the suppressor onto the DUAL-LOK muzzle device and tighten it firmly by hand, with moderate effort.
Turn the collar clockwise or counter-clockwise until it springs rearward over the tines, its rear face flush with the rear face of the tines.
Fire 30 rounds through it to blow out any solvent left inside.
fncheck: Rifle still unloaded: the collar sits flush with the rear face of the tines and the pin is in the left or right side of the U-shaped DUAL-LOK slot — with the can tight, only one side will lock. If the can is going on a host for the first time, confirm alignment before the first shot: Griffin's check rod goes down the can's bore into the barrel until it is flush with the end cap and must not touch the suppressor; remove the rod before shooting. A rod that touches means a gunsmith, typically for the threads.
